author: dgramop
body:
## **PR Description** ### Abstract & description of ADOA as a direction-finding approach We implement a naive approach to Amplitude Difference of Arrival with several simplifying assumptions. Amplitude Difference of Arrival attempts to geo-position a transmitter by looking solely at how the amplitude changes as a function of receiver location. Playing "hot-and-cold" is itself the most naive possible implementation of ADOA, where finite difference can be employed to figure out what direction the signal of interest is coming from. But brining in a solver and doing some math can actually tell us even more information than just hot-and-cold. We know that, over long distances, signals propagate according to the inverse square law. The free-space path-loss (FSPL) formula is specialization of this law to electromagnetic signals propagating in free space. FSPL is a function of distance, parameterized by frequency. Since we know the frequency, we can start solving for distance. If we know the distance from each measurement point, we can draw 3 circles and see where they intersect, and find the transmit power of the transmitter. Unfortunately we don't know the distance. But as we take more measurements, a small number of distances actually would create intersections of the circles. If we take a system of such free-space path loss equations, we can solve them for the following parameters: - Near intersection point (x, y) - Transmit power ### Under the hood We expect such a transmitter to be non-cooperative, and used primarily for communications or jamming. For this reason, we believe a rolling max-hold approach will give us a relatively consistent measurement of transmit power, regardless of transmitter intermittence or symbols being transmitted. We use a Gauss-Newton numeric solver that minimizes the least-squares error for the circle-near-intersection problem (described in abstract) In particular, the solver finds solutions to the path-loss formula in decibels, varying $txpower_{predicted}$ and transmitter position until we have a relatively consistent set of circles: In particular it tries to solve the following equation $$ txpower_{predicted} - fspl_{100MHz}(distanceTo_{measurementLocation}(emitterX_{predicted}, emitterY_{predicted})) = rxpower_{measured} $$ $$ => txpower_{predicted} - fspl_{100MHz}(distanceTo_{measurementLocation}(emitterX_{predicted}, emitterY_{predicted})) - rxpower_{measured} = 0 $$ Of course there will be error in the $rxpower_{measured}$ measurement itself, and error from the simplifying assumptions that allow us to use FSPL. So a vector of such equations will be non-zero, but as we find better predictions the vector will reduce in norm. Since we can compute the Jacobean by hand or by a systems solver, this makes a good candidate for the Gauss-Newton solver, but we don't have to be married to this solver if it means involving a more accurate modeling engine that may not be so trivially differentiable. The differentiability however allows for efficient solution finding with fast convergence Note: for readability, I reduced "constants" (parameters that are not solved for) to function parameters (subscript on the functions). ### Stuff to explore later We note that incorrect solver approaches actually did better when no logarithms were involved. This is somethin There are several [simplifying assumptions (hedgedoc)](https://hedgedoc.foxhunter.ai/jnU7qtoGSaG4GINC19CcgA) made for this naive approach. Some of them may be somewhat necessary limitations for "single player mode" (i.e. where there is only one receiver) and that may be addressable once receivers can share measurement information. With regard to directionality, some amount of super-naive hot-and-cold could actually help initialize the solver and push initial guesses into the direction we expect a solution to be, to prevent the solver from converging to the "blown up solution"

## **How was this PR tested?** I wrote some test cases that profile some of the forward-error made by the solver with the equations I supplied it. Since we do a number of "extra" floating-point operations to improve readability and verification of correctness, this is an avenue for reducing error. However the larger sources of error here are likely the underlying model and other constraints we can put on the solver to encourage it to converge correctly. ![Solver noise sensitivity for solutions inside polygon formed by measurement locations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89de6c65-373f-4888-a643-9fcd29915003) This case has measurements taken from 100-200 meters of the transmitter, all around the transmitter (see measurements_interior) More concerning still is that the solver does not converge (due to a non-invertible matrix) for certain position configurations of receivers, at certain transmitter locations. We should study this more carefully, and I think a heat map that indicates error (or non-convergence) over some bounding box around a straight-line of measurement locations (see fspl_initial_conditions() and note that its convergence can fail if the transmitter is moved still-nearby but closer to the middle of the receiver array in the x-axis). Take for example (100,50) ### Blowing-up issue (From my original hedgedoc:) The solver sometimes likes to blow up the circles to make artficial near-intersection points far, far, far away from the centers of the circles. This corresponds to usually infeasable reception scenarios. We should bound the max anticipated transmit power of the source transmitter. And if the circles get truly “blown up”, it may show that the signal has gotten stronger over distance. That is to say, we should enforce that the path loss is positive, i.e. that the multiplier on the rx_dbm adjustment factor is at least 1 ### Interior-solutions only It also doesn't help that the initial guess is placed at the geometric center of the measurement points, since this encourages finding solutions within the convex hull of the measurement points instead of searching for viable solutions outside the hull ### Precision considerations I suspect the taking of logarithms is seriously hurting our ability to accurately converge, and possibility convergence at all. An accidental approach that used the wrong path loss formula managed to converged accurately even to transmitter positions that were placed outside the receiver convex hull (though the same incorrect formula was applied in the simulator). We could use $rx_{microwatts} = 10^{rx_{dbm}/10}$ as our basis for relative ranging. Then the solver would only really be multiplying/dividing our new $rx_{microwatts}$ "psuedoranges" instead of doing this additively and taking logs. Of course there's also some discussion in code and in hedgedoc of dividing the entire equation for farther away measurements since they are more prone to noise. They carry the information: "probably not here", but not with the authority of "definitely exactly this far away" like louder, closer measurements imply. The receiver noise floor could be a good basis to help us tune this factor, or we can just guess the right variable and the solver will take care of the rest ### Android ### Desktop (dsp-runner)

body:
## Summary

Removes the `break-all` class added in #2731, as it doesn't seem to affect how long Chinese modelSpec descriptions are displayed, but causes long English descriptions to break on characters instead of on words. 

Before:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05be3438-ffe3-49f0-b644-ad9ec55e253d)

After:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a67069f-7a76-4754-9f8a-bd060e92f0ff)


## Change Type

Please delete any irrelevant options.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

Test config:

All `npm run test:client` tests pass.

The display of the menu is the same in both desktop and landscape, and across different UI languages.
Tested in Firefox, Edge, Chrome.

Tested with the following config:

```yaml
modelSpecs:
  list:
    - name: claude-3-5-sonnet
      label: Claude
      description: Claude is an equally capable alternative to ChatGPT, with a different personality and approach to conversation
      preset:
        endpoint: anthropic
        model: claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
        modelLabel: Claude
    - name: gpt-4o
      label: ChatGPT
      description: ChatGPT is great for general conversation and answering questions
      preset:
        endpoint: openAI
        model: chatgpt-4o-latest
        modelLabel: ChatGPT
    - name: o1-preview
      label: GPT-o1
      description: GPT-o1 is good at performing complex reasoning. It's slower and more verbose than ChatGPT.
      preset:
        endpoint: openAI
        model: o1-preview
        modelLabel: GPT-o1
    - name: "gemini"
      label: "Gemini"
      description: 该模型能够同时处理文本、图像、音频、视频和代码等多种数据类型，并具备生成高质量代码的能力。
```

body:
This just updates the postgres dialect definition to add support for the json_object syntax added in https://github.com/apache/datafusion-sqlparser-rs/pull/1507

The syntax was initially added for mssql but also works in postgres

See https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-json.html

See https://github.com/apache/datafusion-sqlparser-rs/issues/1545

support for `json_object('k' VALUE 'v')` is implemented [in a separate PR](https://github.com/apache/datafusion-sqlparser-rs/pull/1547)

A couple of spectests were failing when "hash" was used with named arguments, like so:

  $ ./rakudo-j -e 'say hash(a => 1)'
  Unexpected named argument 'a' passed

Removing the multi sub added with f725f5f4bd for the JVM backend fixes the problem. AFAIU the wrong multi was used, because named arguments weren't taken into account during multi dispatch.

author: jbruechert
body:
Fixes https://github.com/motis-project/motis/issues/671

The fundamental issue is that the GTFS file specifies a 59 second headway, which will be converted to minute granularity by dividing by 60. The / operator on integers truncates towards zero, so we end up with a 0 headway. 

This then makes `number_of_iterations` divide by zero.

for exact_times != 1, properly rounding should be good enough as long as we don't end up with zero.

author: ezesosa
body:
Se implementó la funcionalidad para obtener un **reporte de los pedidos según su estado filtrados por fecha de inicio y fecha de fin**. Como parámetros de la request necesitamos la fecha de inicio (`dateFrom`) y la fecha de fin (`dateTo`). La respuesta que obtendríamos sería un JSON con este formato:

```
{
    "inProgressOrders": 11,
    "finishedOrders": 1,
    "inDeliveryOrders": 1,
    "deliveredOrders": 4,
    "cancelledOrders": 2,
    "totalOrders": 19
}
```
Creo que a partir de esta información podemos elaborar un gráfico en el front utilizando alguna librería.

## Stored Procedures

Para la realización de este reporte se implementaron procedimientos almacenados. Esto significa que, para poder utilizar esta funcionalidad, es necesario acceder al archivo [package.sql](src/main/resources/package.sql) y ejecutar la creación del procedimiento almacenado. Desconozco si esto se puede automatizar --seguramente.

En cuanto al flujo de ejecución, creé una clase que ejecute de manera **genérica** procedimientos almacenados utilizando el nombre del procedimiento, los parámetros de entrada y los parámetros de salida. Para estos últimos dos elementos necesitamos utilizar un **LinkedHashMap** para mantener el orden de los pares clave-valor --el orden de parámetros en los SP es fundamental.

De esta forma, el flujo es el siguiente:

```
Controller --> Service --> Wrapper del ejecutor --> Ejecutor genérico
```

El ejecutor genérico devuelve un map con los parámetros de salida de SQL (configurados en el SP) y, a través de ellos, buildeamos la respuesta de la misma manera en la que venimos trabajando (con un _record_). 

Cabe destacar que, si bien es posible manejar los procedimientos a través de anotaciones, éstas deben colocarse sobre la entity por lo que, a mi parecer, ensuciaría el trabajo que venimos haciendo con la aplicación.

author: sean-prz
body: - closes #251 ## What #### Making the rectangles clickable so that they have the same behaviour as the markers. ## How ### Simplifying the map screen. This PR removes the three states used to manage the life cycle of a preview cards. The listener on `MapIdleCallback` has been removed, removing the need to manage it, making `cancelables` and `removeViewAnnotation` useless. The Preview card lifecycle is now easier to manage. ```patch - var removeViewAnnotation = remember { true } - var cancelables = remember { Cancelable {} } - var listener: MapIdleCallback? ``` Before : On click, the boolean state is set to true, then a mapIdleCallback is created, and when it triggers, it recreate a card, then when the user move, the listener has to be canceled and the boolean set back to false. Instead : A Preview Card is drawn on Click and removed when a movement is detected. _(In depth: This simplification was made possible by moving the .`removeAllViewAnnotation` from a listener on the camera state to a listener on movement.)_ ### Modifying the signature of DrawRectangles Instead of taking a list of location it now takes a list of Parking, because for the preview Card we need all the Parking data. ```patch * Draw the rectangles on the map * * @param polygonAnnotationManager the polygon annotation manager - * @param locationList the list of locations to draw + * @param parkingsList the list of locations to draw */ fun drawRectangles( polygonAnnotationManager: PolygonAnnotationManager?, plabelAnnotationManager: PointAnnotationManager?, - locationList: List + parkingsList: List ) {..} ``` ### Copying the marker click listener for polygon click listener Once these changed have been made, it was just a copy/paste of the listener on click markers. ### Moving the annotationManager into the viewmodel Finally the annotationManager has been moved in the viewmodel so that if a composable need later to launch an action on the preview Card, it can. This change was made to enable the My location button to remove the preview Card ## Why #### Making the rectangles clickable match the expected behaviour, if the markers are clickable there are no reasons why rectangles should not be. -- - ## Code coverage - **MapViewModel**: 84% - **MapScreen** : 77% (Listener on rectangles not tested, like the one on marker click :/ )

author: speederx
body:
## Related issue
Issue reported here #16805
## Changes rationale
To handle `updateOn` setup with `blur` value, the following changes have been made:
1. Adapting the `onInputBlur` conditionally calling `onModelTouched` only if `forceSelection` is `false`.
2. Adding `onModelTouched` call in the `onSelect` ( unconditionally ), which provides the `FormControl` / `FormGroup` the value selected by the user, without considering the text input the user is searching ( unless forceSelection is false ).

## Additional notes

This way was chosen because [NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR](https://angular.dev/api/forms/ControlValueAccessor#registerOnTouched) updates the ancestor calling `registerOnTouched` which by angular docs:

> When implementing registerOnTouched in your own value accessor, save the given function so your class calls it when the control should be considered blurred or "touched"

If `forceSelection` is set to `false` and `updateOn` is set as `blur`, upon  both user input text / search and when user selects an option, the `FormControl` and `FormGroup` will be updated.

author: ususdei
body:
Hi everyone!

I'm currently working on a rust library for a protocol which runs on plain ethernet using a custom ethertype (TECMP on 0x99FE).
It also uses an additional IP-based protocol for discovery and configuration.

I would also like to use this library on some STM32, so I tried to port it from native linux sockets to the smoltcp stack.

Thus I started to implement some basic support for raw ethernet sockets.
This is still a _work in progress_ but the basic functionality already works on an STM32F7.
It is still missing support for Metadata and the send API could be more convenient
but I would like to get this out there and gather some early feedback as to whether you would even consider merging something like this.

So just some initial questions:

- Is this feature even in scope for the smoltcp project?
- Do you agree with my overall design?
- Do you already have any other initial feedback?

Thank you all for your feedback and your great contribution to the embedded rust ecosystem!

author: oklopfer
body:
Requires https://github.com/pacstall/pacstall/pull/1271

if a script has `${_archive}` and `_archive=` is not defined:
- if it is a tar archive or zip:
    - replace all instances with `${pkgname~${pkgver}`
    - prefix all `source[0]` entries (as well as `source_*[0]`) with
        - `@${pkgname~${pkgver}::` or
        - `dest@${pkgname~${pkgver}::` if there was a dest prefix before
- otherwise:
    - replace all instances with `${srcdir}`
    
~~Not directly caused by this, but will be more prevalent after:~~
~~the website API should strip out anything before `::` for final source entries, so that repology will be more likely to accept us again.~~

> ~~This should *not* be altered here, as for the default behavior, we want full source entries to be given, so that entries may be parsable to pacstall in the form they would be used to build. Given this, I am also leaning away from making the change in go-srcinfo, and towards only altering it in the final stretch on the website's end.~~

(EDIT: site fix done here https://github.com/pacstall/website/pull/1097)


<details>
<summary>script to convert:</summary>

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3

import glob
import re
import os

def process_pacscript(pacscript_path):
    with open(pacscript_path, 'r') as f:
        content = f.read()
    if '${_archive}' not in content or '_archive=' in content:
        return
    source_pattern = re.compile(r'^(source(?:_[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)?=\(\s*)(.*?)(\s*\))$', re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE)

    def modify_source_block(match):
        opening = match.group(1)
        sources_text = match.group(2)
        closing = match.group(3)
        lines = sources_text.splitlines()
        new_lines = []
        first_entry_modified = False
        for line in lines:
            stripped_line = line.strip()
            if not stripped_line or stripped_line.startswith('#'):
                new_lines.append(line)
                continue
            if not first_entry_modified:
                match_line = re.match(r'^(\s*)(["\']?)(.*?)(["\']?)(,?\s*)$', line)
                if match_line:
                    indent, quote_start, content_line, quote_end, comma = match_line.groups()
                    if '::' in content_line:
                        prefix, suffix = content_line.split('::', 1)
                        new_content = f'{prefix}@${{pkgname}}~${{pkgver}}::{suffix}'
                    else:
                        new_content = f'@${{pkgname}}~${{pkgver}}::{content_line}'

                    new_line = f'{indent}{quote_start}{new_content}{quote_end}{comma}'
                    new_lines.append(new_line)
                    first_entry_modified = True
                else:
                    new_lines.append(line)
                    first_entry_modified = True
            else:
                new_lines.append(line)
        reconstructed_block = f'{opening}' + '\n'.join(new_lines) + f'{closing}'
        return reconstructed_block

    if re.search(r'\.tar|\.zip|\.tgz', content):
        content = content.replace('${_archive}', '${pkgname}~${pkgver}')
        content_new = source_pattern.sub(modify_source_block, content)
    else:
        content_new = content.replace('${_archive}', '${srcdir}')
    if content_new != content:
        with open(pacscript_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write(content_new)
        print(f"Processed {pacscript_path}")
    else:
        print(f"No changes made to {pacscript_path}")

def main():
    pacscript_files = glob.glob('packages/*/*.pacscript')
    for pacscript in pacscript_files:
        process_pacscript(pacscript)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```
</details>

author: freezylemon
body:
Currently, `Parameters` tries to differentiate its states (owned, shared) by setting the `owner` field. With the way the API works at the moment, there really isn't any advantage to this over using different structs for owned, shared, and mutable shared states. It takes up an extra `Rc` and complicates the differentiation between immutable and mutable borrows (since it's all the same type).

I'm also pretty sure that there is some potential for nasty UB via `Stream::parameters` because the returned `Parameters` type can be accessed mutably[^1] even though `Stream` is supposed to be an immutable reference to `AVStream`.

Some notes regarding the new implementation:
- I want to use the pattern `Something` (owned), `SomethingRef`, `SomethingMut` for other wrapper types in the future
- I don't want to use `impl<'a> AsRef<SomethingRef<'a>> for Something` because it returns a `&'b SomethingRef<'a>` with two levels of indirection, which seems unnecessary
- The macros are required to keep the boilerplate under control. I might even want to add more macros to implement common field types and/or traits with less code
- I might add safety docs to `from_raw`. At the moment, the only safety concern is that you need to bound the returned lifetime correctly (since it can otherwise be arbitrarily chosen). The best way to do this is by bounding it on a borrow of another type:
  ```rs
  pub fn something<'s>(&'s self) -> SomethingRef<'s> { /* ... */ }
  ```
- `StreamMut::copy_parameters_from_context` seems a bit unnecessary, but it is more efficient. The old implementation always allocated a new `AVCodecParameters` from a context, and then copied that `AVCodecParameters` into the stream. The new one just uses `parameters_from_context(stream.codecpar, context)` which avoids the in-between step

[^1]: See examples/transcode-x264.rs: `(*ost.parameters().as_mut_ptr()).codec_tag = 0;`

body:
This pull request includes several changes across multiple files to introduce new functionality and improve existing features. The most important changes include adding user management to the `FileController`, renaming and updating the `GameJamController`, and adding a new `SubmissionsController`.

### User Management in `FileController`:

* Added `UserManager<ApplicationUser>` to `FileController` and updated the constructor to include it. (`Controllers/FileController.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fca8bcb78c94b260e2ee963952854537208162e760cf33464bbffe0859fe5c42R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fca8bcb78c94b260e2ee963952854537208162e760cf33464bbffe0859fe5c42R20-R27)
* Updated `UploadFile` method to include `UserId` and `UploadedDate` in the `GameInformation` object. (`Controllers/FileController.cs` [Controllers/FileController.csL105-R110](diffhunk://#diff-fca8bcb78c94b260e2ee963952854537208162e760cf33464bbffe0859fe5c42L105-R110))

### Renaming and Updating `GameJamController`:

* Renamed `GameJamTestController.cs` to `GameJamController.cs` and updated the class name accordingly. (`Controllers/GameJamController.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355R7-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355L22-R25)
* Added a new `ViewGameJam` method to display game jam details and user submissions. (`Controllers/GameJamController.cs` [Controllers/GameJamController.csR51-R105](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355R51-R105))
* Updated routes and method signatures for `Create`, `Edit`, and `Delete` methods to reflect the new controller name. (`Controllers/GameJamController.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355R122) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355L89-R142) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355L132-R185) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355L149-R202) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355L169-R222) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355L198-R251) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355R265)
* Updated `ToViewModel` method to include new properties and handle null submissions. (`Controllers/GameJamController.cs` [Controllers/GameJamController.csR309-R332](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355R309-R332))

### New `SubmissionsController`:

* Introduced `SubmissionsController` to handle game submissions to game jams, including methods for submitting, viewing, and deleting submissions. (`Controllers/SubmissionsController.cs` [Controllers/SubmissionsController.csR1-R254](diffhunk://#diff-40f18fcc01aa8acb832e873d36b3ce7d2cc83f2161275ac1357df553680fe5ecR1-R254))

### Database Context Updates:

* Added `DbSet<SubmissionsModel>` to `ApplicationDbContext` and defined relationships between models. (`Data/ApplicationDbContext.cs` [Data/ApplicationDbContext.csL15-R45](diffhunk://#diff-73c857fa5717f30789b1fab27594b694d56f01e563c18cc1123846a894a93798L15-R45))

### Initial Data Setup:

* Added initial data setup for test users and a template game jam in `ApplicationDbInitializer`. (`Data/ApplicationDbInitializer.cs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-98b5d370ad8dadcabcf0ab23f4903f141a12f1129e6995ac6a3b77cbe238f1f5L3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-98b5d370ad8dadcabcf0ab23f4903f141a12f1129e6995ac6a3b77cbe238f1f5R16-R23)This pull request includes significant changes to the controllers, models, and views in the Jamly project. The most important changes involve adding user management, creating a new submissions controller, and renaming and refactoring existing controllers and view models.

### User Management Enhancements:
* [`Controllers/FileController.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-fca8bcb78c94b260e2ee963952854537208162e760cf33464bbffe0859fe5c42R9): Added `UserManager<ApplicationUser>` to the `FileController` to manage user-related operations and updated the `UploadFile` method to include the `UserId` of the uploader for the game. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fca8bcb78c94b260e2ee963952854537208162e760cf33464bbffe0859fe5c42R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fca8bcb78c94b260e2ee963952854537208162e760cf33464bbffe0859fe5c42R20-R27) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fca8bcb78c94b260e2ee963952854537208162e760cf33464bbffe0859fe5c42L105-R109)

### New Submissions Controller:
* [`Controllers/SubmissionsController.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-40f18fcc01aa8acb832e873d36b3ce7d2cc83f2161275ac1357df553680fe5ecR1-R123): Introduced a new `SubmissionsController` to handle game submissions, including GET and POST actions for creating and viewing submissions.

### Renaming and Refactoring:
* [`Controllers/GameJamController.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355R7-R16): Renamed from `GameJamTestController.cs` and added new methods for viewing game jam details, including user claims and event claims. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355R7-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355L22-R25) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355R51-R78) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-92a385a049d512924d4aae73dc10ab4e2ab96d812ed6afc90fb16b3abf9c6355R286-R293)
* [`ViewModels/GameJamViewModel.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-3787b2e2572c94d3bb9719996c654aeebd257ea7881bd0ea0ff15ce72fa74c1aR2-R4): Renamed from `Models/GameJamViewModel.cs` and added a new property `DescriptionHtml` for HTML formatted descriptions and a navigation property for submissions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3787b2e2572c94d3bb9719996c654aeebd257ea7881bd0ea0ff15ce72fa74c1aR2-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3787b2e2572c94d3bb9719996c654aeebd257ea7881bd0ea0ff15ce72fa74c1aR19) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3787b2e2572c94d3bb9719996c654aeebd257ea7881bd0ea0ff15ce72fa74c1aR42-R45)

### Database and Model Updates:
* [`Data/ApplicationDbContext.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-73c857fa5717f30789b1fab27594b694d56f01e563c18cc1123846a894a93798L15-R16): Added a new `DbSet<SubmissionsModel>` for managing submissions.
* [`Models/GameInformationModel.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-dcd9f922b530f2588eded32e78968057d7d98fdcd7a85a51cdaf624955be7fc5L1-R5): Updated to include a foreign key to `ApplicationUser` for tracking the creator of the game. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dcd9f922b530f2588eded32e78968057d7d98fdcd7a85a51cdaf624955be7fc5L1-R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dcd9f922b530f2588eded32e78968057d7d98fdcd7a85a51cdaf624955be7fc5L15-R23)
* [`Models/SubmissionsModel.cs`](diffhunk://#diff-d15c16c96098eccb0939c579e5fd6269726f5a6d92c86c55ef2e736a634764b6L20-R31): Added foreign keys for `GameInformationModel` and `ApplicationUser` to link submissions to users and games. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d15c16c96098eccb0939c579e5fd6269726f5a6d92c86c55ef2e736a634764b6L20-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d15c16c96098eccb0939c579e5fd6269726f5a6d92c86c55ef2e736a634764b6L38)

### Dependency Updates:
* [`Jamly.csproj`](diffhunk://#diff-bea00e4c15659001b6cf1e039cf0b2efd5a99d18283bf9ab21f581c5cfacb4ceR13): Added a new package reference for `Markdig` to support Markdown to HTML conversion.

This allows the caller to choose whether to pass instruction parameters directly or load them from buffer account. As a result, we can increase inner message size in Across+. The implementation optimizes for path where parameters are passed directly as that is also simpler for caller to execute.

Currently this change is applied to fill and slow fill methods, but we might want to apply it also on relayer refund leaf execution.

author: rob--w
body:
test/unit/api_spec.js is the only JS file in the tree with trailing whitespace. Because [`trim_trailing_whitespace = true` in .editorconfig](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/d45a61b579df021b65d1f924a1ad864c58407b09/.editorconfig#L10), any editor supporting EditorConfig would trim whitespace when the file is changed, which results in test failures (e.g. at https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/19074#discussion_r1850235715).

This commit fixes the issue by trimming the trailing whitespace and adjusting the test expectations.

The test was originally introduced in https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/16559 and I don't expect any impact on the validity of the test.

author: flynnoconnell
body:
Basic install steps for `venv` working locally.

# Tests:

- [x] Linux venv
- [x] Linux miniforge
- [x] Windows venv
- [x] Windows miniforge

May deprecate miniconda and/or all non-miniforge conda distributions.

# Updates:
1. Build passes on linux, fails on windows. I think this is because CaImAn requires tensorflow >= `v2.4`, which is available on `conda-forge` linux but Windows is only `v1.17`
[TF untested on conda](https://www.tensorflow.org/decision_forests/known_issues#untested_for_conda)
[conda-forge TF versions](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/tensorflow)

Maybe we can skip conda-forge tensorflow and if on windows, install via pip:
```bash
 if [[ "${{ matrix.os }}" == "windows" ]]; then
            pip install tensorflow>=2.4.0
 fi
 ```

Nope. Install still fails even if tensorflow is already installed via Pypi. 

Build works with channels `conda-forge, defaults` and `channel_priority=flexible`!
